record.paper_title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing
record.original_question: If every 4-vertex subset of a 3-tournament contains at least two triples with the same root, must the tournament have domination number at most 2014?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.3. If any four vertices of a 3-tournament T3 n contain at least two triples with the same root then dom(Tn) ≤ 2014.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A 3-tournament on a finite vertex set $V$ is a complete 3-uniform hypergraph on $V$ in which every 3-element edge $\{x,y,z\}$ has a distinguished vertex called its root (or tail). For a vertex subset $S \subseteq V$, say that $S$ dominates the 3-tournament if for every vertex $v \in V \setminus S$ there exists an edge $\{u_1,u_2,v\}$ whose root lies in $S$. The domination number $\mathrm{dom}(T)$ is the minimum cardinality of a dominating set.

Suppose $T$ is a 3-tournament on $n$ vertices with the property that every 4-element subset of $V$ contains (at least) two of its four induced 3-edges that share the same root. Must $\mathrm{dom}(T) \le 2014$?
artifact.status_search_result: Korándi and Sudakov (arXiv:1602.01697, 2016) refuted this conjecture by constructing 3-tournaments of arbitrarily large domination number in which every 4-vertex subset contains at least two triples sharing the same root. Hence the answer is no.

status_evidence.title: Domination in 3-tournaments (Korándi, Sudakov)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs 3-tournaments of arbitrarily large domination number such that any four vertices induce at least two edges with the same tail, refuting the conjectured constant bound.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that the stated condition forces dom(T) ≤ 2014 is false.

status_evidence.title: Domination in 3-tournaments (PDF)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper by Korándi and Sudakov resolving Gyárfás's conjectures on 3-tournament domination.
status_evidence.claim: Refutes the bounded-domination conjecture under the same-root condition.
